title: Saviors of Kamigawa: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "The strain upon the veil between worlds began to show near the end of the Kami War. Strange happenings that neither side could control lashed out across Kamigawa." —*Observations of the Kami War*
"My finest creations are fashioned after the moths of Eiganjo. They fly higher, faster, and more gracefully than any of my own designs." —Noboru, master kitemaker
All bow at its visitation—some in awe, some in honor, some in fear.
"Paint gold upon the wind, Shape the wind into a shield, And vanish behind the brightness." —Snow-Fur, kitsune poet
"The blood of Kiyomaro flows in my veins. He did not let Eiganjo fall and neither shall I."
"The air filled with dust and the sound of wingbeats. The mothriders had joined the fray." —*Great Battles of Kamigawa*
"Do not let a single shaft loose until my word. And when I give that word, do not leave a single shaft in Eiganjo." —General Takeno
"The sword is just a tool. It is the samurai's hand that brings it to life."
"It seems that each time I visit Lord Konda his guards are more on edge, perhaps even more eager for the war to reach them." —Masako the Humorless
"Before the war, we prayed to Kataki to sharpen our swords and harden our armor. Without his blessing our weapons are all but useless against the kami hordes." —Kenzo the Hardhearted
"He kept generations whole before the Kami War, and now he turns his century of wisdom to healing the latest casualties." —Eight-and-a-Half-Tails
"Know your history. The lessons of the past will shield you in times of doubt."
"Watch over my father. Tell him I'm safe, but I won't come home until I find out how to bring him back to his senses, and Kamigawa is again at peace." —Michiko Konda, last letter to General Takeno
"Night wings sprinkled with dust Of a thousand soldiers dead And a thousand cities fallen." —Snow-Fur, kitsune poet
The paths of the kami crisscrossed Kamigawa like scars left by a maddened surgeon.
"Humbly I bow. Silently I wait. Deeply I listen."
"I am not afraid to die today nor afraid of what death will bring."
"Despite the massive forces that allied against him, Konda never once believed he would lose the Kami War." —Masako the Humorless
"The more kami that passed through the veil that separated them from our world, the weaker that veil became, threatening to tear into tatters at the slightest pressure." —*The History of Kamigawa*
"Soramaro speaks through me. Listen! And I will tell the wisdom of the ancestors."
"Be careful where your mind wanders. Even in the quietest moments, the kami are listening, and your thoughts give them shape." —Lady Azami
When a strong mind moves, form and energy shift to heed it.
The apprentice stared in puzzlement. "But Master, you finished writing those spells just yesterday. Don't you remember?" The jushi's heart froze.
"He's a lot like me, that masterless little kami . . . unimpressed by grandeur and never at a loss for a trick." —Toshiro Umezawa
It's dangerous indeed to be lost in someone else's thoughts.
The scrollkeepers never stepped an inch away from the doors of the Great Library, not even when the ogres and their oni masters swept through Minamo.
Like pools of fog that hid treacherous rocks from sailors' eyes, so too were the hands of the kami.
"I feel their unnatural influence in the weary, weeping land. Do they care nothing for the creatures who walk below their clouds?" —Eight-and-a-Half-Tails
When Minamo was abandoned, its younger students found themselves thrust into a war beyond their skill with talents beyond their control.
"My brain hurts."
Cut off from the kakuriyo by the destruction of their honden, the zubera sought new ways to bring their secrets home.
It is all the things that humanity was not meant to know.
"Stand back. I know just what to do." —Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker
Some of Minamo's students claimed he was as old as the knowledge he dispensed.
Sometimes you have to search for inspiration, and sometimes it's right there in front of you.
"Life is a series of choices between bad and worse." —Toshiro Umezawa
Takenuma was filled with a chorus of moans, shrieks, and wails. Some came from the living, some from the dying, and some, most horribly, from the dead.
"We had him cornered, we did . . . and, well, you know what they say about rats." —Araba patrol survivor
In the case of violent deaths, kami offered a chance for revenge if the deceased offered up its corpse as a host to the invading kami.
Nezumi insect-shamans enjoyed solitary lives, which was fortunate since no other nezumi could stand to live within half a mile of their foul stench.
"The sword is just a tool. It is the samurai's hand that delivers death."
The kirin bellowed—an echoing, twisted parody of its once-inspirational call.
The mist was thick, cloying, and constricting. Shiro fought his way to fresh air only to look back and see his comrades fallen on the battlefield behind him.
"Me? No, I'm not going to kill you. I won't even lay a finger on you. I promise." —Kiku, Night's Flower
Simple bargains are the most tempting, and oni bargains are the simplest of all: eternal life for eternal service.
"They're numerous, attack in swarms, and are always hungry. No wonder we rats hold such a kinship with them."
When nothing remains, everything is equally possible.
It gnashed its teeth, and the battlefield filled with the screech of blade striking blade.
"Your blood I'll use. Your skull I'll keep."
"Beware Adamaro! In him all pain and anger is perfected." —Isao, Enlightened Bushi
"What part of 'hayaku ikee!' did you not understand?"
"I lost my hounds in the war and thus found myself employing akki as servants. I found their training to be remarkably similar." —Kensuke, houndmaster
"Kills and cooks your food in one easy stroke."
They moved like apes, but a thousand times swifter, prying into every corner, leaving pawprints of ash.
Wherever it looked, it saw destruction—the wake of its own gaze.
"Through the veil's rip spilled hundreds of minor kami, rushing over the battlefield like embers from a kicked campfire. Then they were gone." —*Great Battles of Kamigawa*
Godo trained their muscles and honed their skills, but he left their hearts wild and empty.
Hidetsugu never relinquished a grudge. He let it burn within him, gathering ever greater intensity until the final moment of vengeance.
"Heart of Sokenzan, I call to you! Lend me your fire."
The oni leapt easily from peak to peak, toying with its victims, its voice a purr from the rumbling depths of nightmare.
"Walking the path of the kami only leaves you with singed feet." —Soratami saying
The akki were surprised to encounter a human who could fight in the caves as well as they.
Its fiery visitation burns away the fog of war and dissipates the ties of loyalty.
The akki knew to stay indoors on the days the oni flew their kites.
Trapped for eons within the sacred gong, the kami boomed and clanged to a deafening tempo as they destroyed their erstwhile prison.
"In our war with the kami, we annihilate what is our own. Do they too suffer ruination in their hidden world?" —Diary of Azusa
Before Shinka's walls were built, before the torii at Okina stood, she was there, tall and proud against the sky, and she will be there long after they have fallen into dust.
Even the most benevolent and life-giving of kami joined the war against the mortal world, but only with heavy and sorrowful hearts.
One thorn to warn, ten thorns to defend, a hundred thorns to destroy.
The orochi learned how to move swiftly and surely along the forest floor, like fish darting through gull-watched waters.
As Dosan's chant grew in volume, a second, deeper voice rose up in harmony behind it, strong enough to shake the earth and yet vibrant enough to fill the spirit.
"Like a riddle, it unwinds. Like a green wind, it reaches out. Like a sudden guilt, it seizes." —Snow Fur, kitsune poet
The ghostly objects around the kami circled faster and faster, creating a dizzying cyclone of motion. When it opened its eyes, it struck.
"In the waning moments of war, humanity's most ancient ancestors return. But whose side shall they make their own?" —Isao, Enlightened Bushi
"We have learned much from the orochi."
Only the most skilled budoka could protect the Okina Shrine. Only the best of these protectors took the night watch.

"After his death, monks spent ten years transcribing the tattoos from Reki's body and gathering stories from those who spoke with him. Thus the volume you hold was written." —*The History of Kamigawa*

"Scouts of the Sakura Tribe spent two years wandering the forest to learn every leaf and tree. That knowledge was called upon during the Kami War to ensure the orochi's survival." —*The History of Kamigawa*
With a sadness and a sense of hope, Senka left the colony of her birth and, with her attendants, set out to serve as broodmistress, founder of a new colony.
"I've seen this great land from every angle. I know its every tree, stone, and river bend. Yet I have come to realize that knowing a thing is not the same as healing it." —Diary of Azusa
The ashes of the dead mingle with the soil, and both become as one.
In an age of war, time is measured not by sand but by blood.
"Owls filled the skies during the Kami War, harbingers of darker times to come." —*The History of Kamigawa*
It is said that the feathers of a crane are clouds, plucked and sewn together by the hands of the kami.
The words from which language sprang, the knowledge from which thought was born, the story from which history was woven.
Godo never revealed what went into his special brew, but he always had more of it after great victories.
"Center of the Sea, Eye of the World, Shrine of Enlightenment. Seek it for answers. Seek it for healing. Seek it and return transformed." —Scroll fragment from the ruins of Minamo
Here the soratami wove their endless plots—graceful, artful, and deceitful, while the unwitting world moved below.
